name: The Threadfall Markets (Migrant Bazaar Circuit)
description: Unlike fixed ghost markets, Threadfall operates as a moving circuit of pop-up bazaars that follow a loose seasonal calendar across Tier 1 and Tier 2 zones, announced only through encrypted BCI whisper-threads that dissolve sixty seconds after reading. Vendors — many of them licensed nowhere — offer geneware offcuts, unlicensed BCI firmware, hand-cultivated food, and contraband aesthetics from corponation supply chains. The most celebrated iteration, the Solstice Threadfall, has occupied a different condemned structure each year since 2207, drawing crowds of two thousand into spaces that officially don't exist. Enforcement sweeps have never caught the market mid-operation; the consensus is that at least three GLMZ Transit Authority officers are on the circuit's informal payroll.
cultural_impact: Threadfall has become a low-tier institution for accessing goods and community outside corporate retail infrastructure, and the whisper-thread invitation system has been copied by dozens of unrelated underground networks across M88.
locations: Rotating through condemned Shelf blocks 14-F through 22-C
Former Kurosawa-Petrov Logistics depot, South Corridor
story_hooks: A journalist with a Tier 3 outlet receives a Threadfall whisper-thread by mistake — or was it a mistake?
The Solstice Threadfall is raided for the first time in its history; someone inside the circuit sold the location, and the vendors want to know who.
A rare geneware sample circulating at Threadfall is traced back to a sealed corporate research program that officially ended in 2198.
